To support the current approaches of diagnostic management (like software updates), two architecture approaches are possible: • Each SoftwareCluster has its own diagnosticAddress and Diagnos- ticContributionSet . • Multiple SoftwareCluster share the diagnosticAddress and also the Di- agnosticContributionSet . For details on the semantics and precise configuration of SoftwareCluster s, see [23]. DM is intended to support an own Diagnostic Server instance per Diag- nosticContributionSet . All Diagnostic Server instances share the same UDS TransportLayer (see Figure 7.1) and each Diagnostic Server manages its own resources. [SWS_DM_00420] Instantiation of Diagnostic Server Status: DRAFT Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04216 ⌈ DM shall instantiate an independent Diagnostic Server per DiagnosticContribu- tionSet , which is referenced by one or multiple SoftwareCluster s in the role of diagnosticExtract , with dedicated resources and functionality configured by this DiagnosticContributionSet . ⌋ Details on required configuration items are described in section 7.3.5. This chapter focuses on requirements concerning a single Diagnostic Server, hence we assume that • requests from Diagnostic Clients are already dispatched towards this Diagnostic Server according to [SWS_DM_00390] and [SWS_DM_00391], • DEXT configuration elements used in a requirement are meant to be part of the DiagnosticContributionSet associated to the Diagnostic Server according to [SWS_DM_00420]. In particular, we note that requests addressing different Diagnostic Server in- stances shall be processed independently by the respective Diagnostic Servers. Specification of Diagnostics AUTOSAR AP R25-11 Most interaction between DM and application is realized by instances of ara::diag classes. The application instantiates the ara::diag objects and uses the provided in- terface to interact with the DM. The application itself can be deployed anywhere. They can run in the local SoftwareCluster , but also remote on other SoftwareClus- ter s or even other hardware is possible. 7.3.1.1 MetaInfo class The ara::diag::MetaInfo class specifies a mechanism to provide meta infor- mation, i.e. from transport protocol layer, to an interested application. To support this, ara::diag::MetaInfo::GetValue is specified, which provides the accord- ing value represented as a ara::core::StringView . The context of the current request may also be retrieved by an application by calling ara::diag::MetaInfo::Get- Context . The context of a request could be either kDiagnosticCommunication , kFaultMemory or kDoIP . The detailed information on meanings of the context and key-value pairs can be looked up in Table 7.1 “MetaInfo type definition”.

Table 7.1: MetaInfo type definition For context kDoIP none of the listed keys is applicable. 7.3.1.1.1 Provision of MetaInfo [SWS_DM_02094] Provision of source address Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04170 ⌈ The DM shall provide the source address (SA) of the diagnostic client from which the diagnostic request was received within metaInfo using the Key kSA in all the subse- quently called ara::diag interfaces. ⌋ [SWS_DM_02095] Provision of target address Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04170 ⌈ The DM shall provide the target address (TA) of the diagnostic server to which the diagnostic request was sent within metaInfo using the Key kTA in all the subsequently called ara::diag interfaces. ⌋ [SWS_DM_02096] Provision of UDS addressing mode Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04170 ⌈ The DM shall provide the UDS addressing mode (TAType) of the diagnostic request (physical or functional) within metaInfo using the Key kTAType in all the subsequently called ara::diag interfaces. ⌋ 114 of 1171 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics

Specification of Diagnostics AUTOSAR AP R25-11 7.3.1.1.2 Lifetime of MetaInfo [SWS_DM_01345] Lifetime of MetaInfo Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04170 ⌈ For each method called from DM to application with a MetaInfo as parameter, the DM shall limit the guaranteed life time of the MetaInfo object only to the time that function call is active. ⌋ Note: An example of a method call with MetaInfo as parameter is [SWS_DM_00618]. In general the callee is not supposed to store or reuse the MetaInfo object after the DM function has returned. This would result in undefined behavior. 7.3.1.2 Concurrency of ara::diag interfaces Some constructors of ara::diag interfaces accepts an parameter of type ara::diag:: ConcurrencyType which allows an AA developer to inform the DM if the callback(s) API is implemented in a thread-safe manner or not. If the ara::diag::Concurren- cyType is set to kConcurrent , then DM can invoke the API multiple times without waiting for the previous invocation to deliver the final result. In case the ara::diag:: ConcurrencyType is set to kNotConcurrent , DM will block the request till the result of the ongoing request is fully delivered (Status of the future returned is ready). The usage of ara::diag::ConcurrencyType is only limited to the APIs imple- mented by an AA. All the other APIs have their thread-safety specified in the API description. 7.3.1.3 Caching of application calls An application can call a ara::diag method call at any point in time and independent from the current state of the DM process itself. For the application calling such a function it is unknown if the DM is actually currently available or not. Typical examples are: • At startup the application is up and running and reporting information but the DM is not yet started and likely be up shortly after the call • The communication between the ara::diag interface and the DM itself is temporar- ily interrupted If the application would need to handle these situations to react on the not available DM, they would get very complex. Furthermore, each and every application would need to implement a complex strategy. To avoid this and to ease the interaction between application and DM for these functions, the ara::diag methods where the application calling the DM outside of service processing, the DM caches the relevant information and forwards this data to the DM instance once it is available. If any ara::diag::SovdServiceValidation::Validate returns an error any contained resource, then the DM shall immediately return an error to the client and not proceed processing the request any further. ⌋ 7.3.3.3 SOVD Data Serialization & Data Conversion The exchange of data from a SOVD Client to a SOVD Server and vice versa takes place on an interpreted physical level, whereas internally (as well as for UDS ISO 14229-1 [1]) the data is expressed by internal data types. The data is defined by DiagnosticSovdContentElement and aggregated by DiagnosticSovd- Content . To express this transformation SwDataDefProps are aggregated by DiagnosticSovdContentElement . This section describes how these transformations shall be interpreted for SOVD and how the subset of a JSON schema that represents a DiagnosticSovdContent shall be derived based on Diagnostic Extract Template[4], so that the Diagnostic Server instance can offer consistent ASAM SOVD [5] [14] [13] APIs. 7.3.3.3.1 SOVD Data – Serialization SOVD data is serialized, using settings from DiagnosticSovdProps.singleEle- mentSerialization . The setting object is supported by this version of the stan- dard. See also chapter Common primitive data types in ISO 17978-3(2026) [13]. 7.3.3.3.2 SOVD Data – Conversion [SWS_DM_01465] SOVD data representation of atomic numeric data Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04256 ⌈ The atomic subset of a SOVD request or response body matching a Diagnos- ticSovdContentElement with DiagnosticSovdPrimitiveContentElement. swDataDefProps with baseTypeEncoding NONE or 2C and a compuMethod of category IDENTICAL , LINEAR , SCALE_LINEAR , RAT_FUNC or SCALE_RAT_FUNC as defined in Diagnostic Extract Template[4] shall be of type integer or number and shall derive the JSON schema properties type , minimum , maximum and mul- tipleOf based on baseTypeEncoding , baseTypeSize , dataConstr and com- puMethod of the corresponding DiagnosticSovdPrimitiveContentElement. swDataDefProps . ⌋ 197 of 1171 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics

Specification of Diagnostics AUTOSAR AP R25-11 It is assumed, that there is only a single proximity_challenge present at any point in time, that is valid for all SOVD clients and all operations . Therefore, a typical application implementing ara::diag::SovdProximityChallenge does not need to manage an individual proximity_challenge for each requested operation and for each client. The lifetime of a proximity_challenge is typically set to a fixed time by the appli- cation (e.g. 2 minutes). If further complexity, such as different proximity_challenges per client are needed, the ara::diag::MetaInfo object can be evaluated by the application, to implement client or operation specific proximity_challenges . But in most cases this will not be necessary. [SWS_DM_01398] Providing the SOVD operation proximity_challenge Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04262 ⌈ If a SOVD operation has DiagnosticSovdOperation.proximityProofRe- quired set to TRUE , in each response body where the attribute proxim- ity_challenge is required, the Diagnostic Server instance shall return the attribute in the response body of the SOVD method with the value returned by ara:: diag::SovdProximityChallenge::GetChallenge . ⌋ [SWS_DM_01397] SOVD operation mode Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04262 ⌈ The SOVD attribute modes of a SOVD operation shall not be supported. ⌋ [SWS_DM_01395] Validation of SOVD operation proximity_response Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04262 ⌈ If a SOVD request body contains a proximity_response , the Diagnostic Server instance shall call the method ara::diag::SovdProximityChal- lenge::ValidateResponse with the parameter proximityResponse set to the con- tent from the request body and consider the proximity_challenge valid, if kProx- imityChallengeValidationSuccessful is returned. ⌋ [SWS_DM_02171] Operation execution without required proxim- ity_challenge Upstream requirements: RS_Diag_04262 ⌈ If a SOVD method to execute an operation is received and the DiagnosticSovd- Operation.proximityProofRequired is set to TRUE and the SOVD request body does not contain a proximity_response , the DM shall deny the request and return an SOVD error 400 (Bad Request). ⌋ 215 of 1171 Document ID 723: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Diagnostics
